ch4_lab_uiux.title: Quick Check: UI vs. UX & Elements of Design

questions.q: A UI Designer asks "Is this beautiful and on-brand?" A UX Designer asks a different question. What is it?
options: "Is this easy? Can the user achieve their goal without thinking?"
"Is this beautiful and on-brand?" -- they ask the same question

questions.q: A designer says a button "needs more contrast" but only changes its hue, not how light or dark it is. Will that fix the contrast problem?
options: Yes, hue changes always fix contrast
Not necessarily -- contrast is primarily a Value problem, not a Color/hue problem
No, contrast can never be fixed with color
Yes, but only for large text

questions.q: In the "Ketchup Bottle" analogy, the glass bottle looks beautiful but requires smacking the bottom to get ketchup out. What does that represent?

ch4_lab_gestalt.title: Quick Check: Gestalt & Core UX Principles

questions.q: A homepage has one big photo on the left and, on the right, a headline plus two paragraphs with breathing room around them. Is this page unbalanced?
options: Yes, it needs a mirror-image layout to be balanced
No -- this is asymmetrical balance, where visual weight is offset without being a mirror image
Yes, only symmetrical layouts count as balanced
Balance doesn't apply to layouts with images

questions.q: Which Gestalt principle explains why navigation links that all share the same color are instantly perceived as "the same kind of thing"?
Showing a "Success" message after a user submits a form is an example of which Core Principle of Good UX?

ch4_lab_colortype.title: Quick Check: Color Theory, Typography & White Space

questions.q: In the 60-30-10 rule, what is the 10% Accent Color reserved for?
options: Whichever color the designer likes best

questions.q: What's the difference between legibility and readability, as the chapter defines them?
options: Legibility is whether letters are distinguishable (a font property); readability is whether a full paragraph is comfortable to read (a layout property)
Legibility only applies to headings; readability only applies to body text
Readability is about color; legibility is about size

questions.q: A complementary color scheme (colors directly opposite on the wheel) is best used for what, according to the chapter?
options: Making one CTA button impossible to miss, via maximum contrast
The safest, most cohesive option for an entire site
